partner_context.their_ambition: The Maldives is the world's benchmark luxury archipelago — 1,200 islands, 160+ resorts, and a tourism economy built on getting affluent guests from the airport to a private island as fast and seamlessly as possible.
partner_context.their_pressure: The transfer experience is the weakest link in a premium stay: seaplanes are weather-limited, daylight-only, loud and carbon-heavy; diesel speedboats are rough and slow. As resorts decarbonize and guests expect more, the legacy transfer fleet has become the bottleneck — and the liability.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier already operates here. The Navier × JIH Global partnership is a live, at-scale deployment turning the transfer layer into a fast, smooth, all-weather, zero-emission foiling network — the proof case the rest of the world now points to.

hero.title: Navier × Maldives — the flagship island-hopping network, live
hero.subtitle: The transfer layer of the world's premier archipelago, re-platformed on foiling-electric vessels.
hero.what_we_do_together: Through the Navier × JIH Global partnership we are deploying a foiling-electric vessel network across the Maldives — replacing rough diesel speedboat transfers and weather-bound seaplane legs with fast, silent, all-weather island-hopping. Navier brings the software-defined fleet, captain training and certification path; the partnership brings the resort relationships, the lagoon-by-lagoon rollout and the national footprint. This is the live case study every other archipelago is now measured against.

why_now: The Navier × JIH Global agreement — ~100 vessels, $100M, a three-year phased rollout with the first 5 boats in 2026 — was reported by The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg in May 2026. It is the largest deployment of foiling-electric vessels in tourism, and it is already underway. The Maldives is no longer a pitch; it is the precedent.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots between the international airport and the resort jetty — the highest-value leg of the journey. A foiling transfer connects Velana International directly to resort lagoons and atoll hubs, with seaplane and domestic-air retained only for the longest outer-atoll legs. Resorts book and brand the experience; guests step from jet to foil to villa.

journeys_unlocked.today: Congested causeway road or a ferry.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A fast foiling commuter and visitor link across the capital's lagoon.

journeys_unlocked.today: A slow tender or a charter booked hours ahead.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: On-demand premium island-hopping between resorts, sandbanks and dive sites — the in-stay water layer.

differentiation.why_navier: The only partner with a live, at-scale foiling-electric network operating in the Maldives today — software-defined, autonomy-ready, supplied from a Turkey factory, and already phasing across atolls under a publicly reported national agreement.

proof_points.claim: The deal is real, public and at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / three-year phasing; first 5 boats in 2026.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

proof_points.claim: The transfer market is large and premium.
proof_points.evidence: 160+ resorts, ~2M annual visitors, nearly all requiring a sea or air transfer on arrival.
The Maldives has a stated net-zero ambition and acute exposure to sea-level rise — a zero-emission transfer fleet is strategically aligned.

objections.concern: Can it handle open-atoll crossings and swell?
objections.response: The foil flies above the chop, delivering a smoother ride than a diesel speedboat in the same conditions; Pioneer II covers intra-atoll legs all-electric, and Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longest outer-atoll crossings with no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: What about charging across remote islands?
objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at resort jetties; Quanta-LR needs no charging at all — exactly the constraint that previously kept electric out of the outer atolls.

No — it complements them. Foiling takes the high-frequency near/mid-atoll legs (all-weather, after-dark, lower cost); seaplanes keep the longest, lowest-frequency outer routes. Together they lift reliability across the whole network.
It is already happening — phased atoll-by-atoll under the JIH Global agreement, with the first vessels arriving in 2026.

close.title: The case the world now points to.
close.body: The Maldives is no longer the pitch — it is the proof. A foiling-electric transfer network at national scale, live and phasing, is the precedent every other luxury archipelago is now measured against.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

end_state.headline: A national foiling transfer layer across the world's benchmark archipelago.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every inhabited and resort atoll in the Maldives — ~26 natural atolls, 160+ resorts and the Greater Malé urban region — connected by a fast, silent, zero-emission foiling network.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II for inner/mid-atoll transfers; Quanta-LR for outer-atoll all-weather crossings
steady_state.tam_framing: ~2M annual visitors, nearly all requiring a transfer — the largest premium marine-transfer market on earth.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is the world's first archipelago-scale foiling network: jet-to-foil-to-villa across the entire Maldivian atoll chain, the live reference case for the planet's island-hopping markets.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.

revenue_potential.anchor_note: $1.1M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total guest journey spend across transport, food, stays, experiences, and ancillary revenue the partner monetizes on-island. Journey GMV rung is in this unit.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

rungs.label: SOM — floor (published)

rungs.label: SOM — full network
rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 10% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market · leading-operator 25% capture, network-wide

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.
